facts.raw_span: A 22-year-old woman
history of systemic lupus erythematosus
fever
Temperature of 101.5°F
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
Several large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Normocytic anemia (mean corpuscular volume: 99 fL; hemoglobin: 11.7 g/dL; hematocrit: 33.4%)
Platelet count: 81 K/μL (thrombocytopenia)
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:1280 (speckled pattern)
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
Dusky malar erythema with focal heme crusting

concepts.why: The patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, and the presence of antinuclear antibody titer and punch biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
The patient presents with erythematous plaques and target lesions, which are characteristic of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient's skin lesions are consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, which is a subtype of cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The presence of bullae and the punch biopsy findings suggest vasculitis, which is a condition characterized by inflammation of blood vessels.
The patient has a low platelet count, which is a common finding in systemic lupus erythematosus.
The patient has normocytic anemia, which is a type of anemia that is commonly seen in chronic diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus.
The punch biopsy findings show dyskeratosis, which is a characteristic feature of cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient's skin lesions show interface dermatitis, which is a characteristic feature of cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
